title: Ranjit Bajaj Drops Out of India U-15 World Cup Role Despite AIFF Appointment
excerpt: The Minerva Academy founder walks away from the team manager position just weeks after the federation named him alongside head coach Bibiano Fernandes for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup.
body:
• Minerva Academy founder Ranjit Bajaj has withdrawn from the India U-15 team manager role for the FIFA U-15 World Cup despite being appointed by the AIFF alongside head coach Bibiano Fernandes.
  • Bajaj had earlier demanded full control of the U-15 squad, including the right to choose his own coaching staff, but was given a manager role under an AIFF-appointed head coach instead.
  • The departure leaves India's preparation in turmoil with the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup just months away.
  • AIFF also gave Jamshedpur FC more time to reconsider their decision to shut down operations, in a separate development.

Ranjit Bajaj, one of Indian football's most vocal youth development advocates, has walked away from the India U-15 World Cup project despite being officially appointed by the All India Football Federation, according to reports from India Today and Firstpost. The decision throws India's preparations for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup into further uncertainty.

From Bold Appeal to Bitter Exit

The departure marks a dramatic reversal. Just weeks earlier, Bajaj had made an impassioned public appeal to AIFF President Kalyan Chaubey, asking for complete charge of the India U-15 team. The Minerva Academy founder, whose youth squads have won titles at the Helsinki Cup, Gothia Cup, and beaten Liverpool's U-15 side 6-0, had promised to deliver a World Cup trophy if given full operational freedom.

"Give me the U-15 team, and I'll bring the trophy home," Bajaj had declared, offering to work without salary or official title in exchange for total authority over player selections and the right to choose his own technical staff.

"Give me the U-15 team, and I'll bring the trophy home. I'm folding my hands and requesting you."

— Ranjit Bajaj, Minerva Academy founder

The AIFF Compromise That Fell Short

The AIFF's response appeared to meet Bajaj halfway. The federation appointed veteran coach Bibiano Fernandes as the U-15 head coach and named Bajaj as team manager, according to Rediff and The Sporting News. Fernandes, a former India U-17 coach who guided the team to AFC U-16 Championship quarter-finals and back-to-back SAFF U-15 titles, brought institutional credibility to the setup.

But for Bajaj, the arrangement fell short of what he had demanded. His original appeal had been explicit: he wanted to lead the team his way, with zero federation interference and full control over coaching appointments. Being placed in a manager role under an AIFF-selected head coach was not the mandate he had sought.

A Pattern of Friction

The fallout is the latest chapter in Bajaj's long-running conflict with Indian football's governing body. The former I-League champion club owner — Minerva Punjab FC won the title in 2017-18, ending Punjab's 21-year wait for a national championship — has been a persistent critic of AIFF's youth development approach. He has accused the federation of prioritizing bureaucracy over results and sidelining people who produce outcomes on the pitch.

Bajaj's academy has produced over 240 international players and operates a fully funded World Cup Batch program offering scholarships to more than 200 young footballers. His long-term vision centers on building a core squad capable of competing at the 2034 FIFA World Cup.

What It Means for India's Campaign

The withdrawal leaves India's U-15 preparations in a precarious position. With the tournament just months away, the team now lacks one of the country's most experienced youth football figures. Fernandes remains in charge as head coach, but the loss of Bajaj's grassroots network and scouting reach — Minerva Academy processes 183,000 applications annually — is significant.

The inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup represents a major opportunity for India to showcase its youth talent on a global stage. Whether the AIFF can rally a cohesive setup in Bajaj's absence will be closely watched by fans who had rallied behind his appointment with a petition that crossed 100,000 signatures.

In a separate decision, the AIFF also granted Jamshedpur FC additional time to reconsider their planned closure, according to Sportstar, as the federation navigates multiple structural challenges ahead of a pivotal year for Indian football.
